summary: The animation basics work: clips are found by name, crossfades and one-shots play, and the quarks bursts fire. But the moments that make the one-projectile loop fun get almost no feedback. There is no hit-stop, camera shake, hit flash or knockback; catching and picking up have no body motion; spawns have no warning; and a dropped projectile makes no sound. Three things look broken, not just plain. (1) The thrown props are modelled upright but scaled by their footprint, so the Rogue's dagger flies as a 3 m pillar, the sword is 2.3 m, the axe 1.1 m and the shield spins edge-on, while the hero keeps holding the same item in hand. (2) Skeletons stay underground for the whole 0.9 s rise, because Spawn_Ground_Skeletons is 3.57 s long, and then pop up already walking. (3) Splitter children use the Ranger hero's model. Feet also slide on the ground: 3x on the hero's run, 15x when running backwards, 6-10x on the skeleton walk. Everything needed is already in the KayKit packs in the scratchpad (Spawn_Ground, Death_C_Skeletons, Hit_B, Running_B, Interact, Taunt). three r169 has no per-bone masks, but supports the two layering tools that matter: track-filtered clips (part 1) and additive clips, which I checked here for hit flinches. Almost all of this is work in render/main/audio/fx plus a few new event fields; the simulation rules stay the same, except one optional balance change that I flag.

recommendations.title: Make the one projectile look like one real object: size, orientation, spin, held/not-held
recommendations.why: The thrown object is the whole game, and right now it looks wrong. The KayKit props are modelled upright (Y-up, no node rotations), and setHero fits them with instance(..., { r: 0.32 }), i.e. by footprint. In flight the dagger becomes 0.64x2.98x0.37 m (a 3 m pillar, taller than the skeletons; confirmed in a headless iPhone-14 screenshot at 10.8 m), the sword 2.26 m tall, the axe 1.11 m (the hero is 1.3 m), and the shield spins on its edge like a coin. For the core rule (one projectile, go get it), the hero keeps holding the same item while it flies: Barbarian 1H_Axe, Knight Round_Shield and Rogue Knife stay visible. So the character never shows 'I am empty-handed'. The 'Крупная пуля' perk (+35% p.r per level) changes nothing on screen. The THREE.Line trail is 1 px wide (iOS ignores linewidth), a hairline on a Retina screen.
recommendations.how:
heroes.js proj: add spin mode + length: barbarian {axe_1handed, spin:'tumble', len:0.75}, knight {shield_round,'disc',0.6}, rogue {dagger,'point',0.6}, ranger {sword_1handed,'whirl',0.9}, stonemage {rock_single_A,'roll'} (rock is flat, keep r 0.32); add heldProp: '1H_Axe' / 'Round_Shield' / 'Knife'.
render.js setHero lines 247-250: instance(kit, model, { height: len }), then center on the box: p.obj.position.sub(new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(p.obj).getCenter(v)) instead of position.y = -0.15. Put it inside an 'align' group: tumble rotation.y = PI/2 (blade plane vertical, along the flight path); disc rotation.x = -PI/2 (lies flat); point/whirl rotation.x = PI/2 (tip forward / flat blade).
sync lines 393-394: take heading from the frame-to-frame change in visual position, so it works for the snake sway, spiral, orbit and bezier paths; spinner.rotation.order = 'YXZ'. tumble: y = heading, x += 20*dt (about 3 rev/s, end over end). disc: y += 18*dt, z = clamp(turnRate*0.12, +-0.35) (tilts into the boomerang's 1.7 rad/s curve, about 12 deg). point: y = heading. whirl: y += 22*dt. roll: x += 7*dt, y += 5*dt. Add proj.group.scale.setScalar(p.r / 0.3).
Held state: hero.heldProp.visible = p.state === 'held'; on catch/pickup/return, pop its scale 0 -> 1.25 -> 1 over 0.18 s. Ranger: put a 0.5x clone of the sword in handslotr. Orb mages: a 0.08 m glowing sphere (MeshBasicMaterial, color x1.6, so it blooms) at the top of the 2H_Staff / 1H_Wand node. Stone mage: the rock above the Spellbook.
Drop: in game.js step, set `const wasFlying = proj.state === 'flying'` after line 121, and after the explosion block emit(g,'drop',{x,z}) when wasFlying and the state is now 'dropped'. Do not push it in weapons.drop(): tests/perks.test.mjs:26 counts every p.events entry (expects 4/5). Render on 'drop': 0.2 s fall from y 0.6 with one bounce; axe/dagger/sword end stuck blade-down at about 35 deg (no bob); the shield ends flat with a coin wobble; keep the bob only for orbs; on ice (rule.dropSlide) the prop lies flat and spins while it slides.
Trail: replace the THREE.Line with a 24-segment ribbon (48 verts, additive, 0.18 m wide at the head tapering to 0); make it gold and 1.6x wider while g.shotMult > 1. In fx.setTrail, pass on = flying && !g.over && !g.choosing; today particles pile up on the frozen projectile behind the perk and game-over screens.

recommendations.title: Kill impact: hit-stop, white flash, directional death and knockback, camera shake, bodies that sink
recommendations.why: A kill with your only projectile is the payoff. Today it is a particle puff, a 0.05 s fade into Death_A (falls 0.26 m backward, on the ground by 0.5 s), and at 1.1 s the body disappears in one frame (dying t:1.1, line 366). There is no freeze, no flash, no camera reaction and no sense of direction. Multi-kills come very fast (sim: ricochet 4 kills in 0.20 s, lightning 6 kills in 0.53 s, black hole 2 kills in the same step), so they blur together.
recommendations.how:
main.js frame(): add freeze/slowT/slowK timers in real time. While freeze>0 the sim dt is 0. After a handle() that starts a freeze, set acc=0 and break out of the step loop. Keep yaw/look and the aim line live. view.sync gets dt (0 during a freeze); fx.update and the shake get real dt, so the burst keeps growing during the freeze. Values in handle(): first kill of a shot 45 ms, later kills within 0.25 s 25 ms (lightning 6-chain = 0.17 s total), combo>=4 slowMo(0.5, 0.3 s), 'explode' 80 ms.
game.js killEnemy line 76: add vx:p.vx, vz:p.vz, px:p.x, pz:p.z to the event.
render.js addEnemyView: clone the materials per enemy (SkeletonUtils.clone shares the 2 MeshStandardMaterials of a model between all copies), emissive white, intensity 0. effect('kill'|'hurt'): v.flash = 1; in sync emissiveIntensity = 1.6*flash, fading over 0.1 s (blooms on 'high'). It stays white during the freeze, which is the classic look.
Knockback: dir = |v|>2 ? v : (enemy - projectile). On death set obj.rotation.y = atan2(-dir.x, -dir.z) (both deaths fall toward -Z), then slide 0.7 m with ease-out over 0.25 s. Big kills (combo>=3, explosion, shield): Death_C_Skeletons (2.0 s; down by 0.3 s, slides itself 1.07 m back by 0.9 s), +0.3 m push and a 0.25 m hop. Replace t:1.1 with age/life: Death_A lies until 0.8 s, sinks at 1.6 m/s, removed at 1.3 s; Death_C removed at 1.6 s; stop the mixer once the clip is clamped.
Tank 'hurt': additive Hit_B over the walk. add = THREE.AnimationUtils.makeClipAdditive(clip.clone()); clone it, because makeClipAdditive edits the clip in place and the loader cache shares GLTF clips between all instances. Then mixer.clipAction(add, undefined, THREE.AdditiveAnimationBlendMode), LoopOnce. Measured: head 52 deg, arm 81 deg, 0.13 m stagger, back to the plain walk (0.0 deg) after 0.87 s, no jump at the start. Lines 373-374: replace the 1.3x inflate with a squash (1+0.25k, 1-0.2k, 1+0.25k).
Shake (end of sync): trauma 0..1, decays 1.8/s, s = trauma^2. After lookAt: rotateX/rotateY(n*0.035*s), rotateZ(n*0.052*s), where n is a two-sine noise at 23-31 Hz (at most 2/2/3 deg). Top view: x0.35, and call placeCamera() every frame there so offsets don't add up. Positional kicks go into camGoal (position is lerped). Trauma: kill 0.3 (+0.1 per combo step, max 0.7), explode 0.6, catch 0.2. Settings toggle «Тряска экрана», off by default under prefers-reduced-motion.
Explosion: an additive ring that expands to the real radius ex.r in 0.25 s; it also shows the player the radius.
Optional (balance call): in game.js damage(), when hp>0 push the tank back 0.45 m along the hit (deterministic).

recommendations.title: Make spawns visible: Spawn_Ground with a ground-crack warning instead of the 3.57 s clip; fix splitter children
recommendations.why: Walkers 'rise' for RISE_TIME 0.9 s, harmless, but play Spawn_Ground_Skeletons, which is 3.57 s long. At 0.9 s the head bone is still 0.19 head-heights underground (hips -0.74). Only a hand shows from about 0.35 s. Then sync crossfades to the walk in 0.2 s, so every skeleton pops out of the floor already walking. The warning the rise is meant to give is invisible, and rising skeletons can be killed while still underground ('+10' out of nowhere). Splitter children are created with the hard-coded hero model 'Rogue_Hooded' (game.js line 79, left over from v1.2), so a Skeleton Mage splits into two copies of the Ranger hero holding all 5 hand props.
recommendations.how:
Re-export the 4 skeleton GLBs from the original pack with scratchpad/gt/pack.mjs: "Skeleton_X:Idle|Walking_D_Skeletons|Running_A|Running_B|Death_A|Death_C_Skeletons|Hit_A|Hit_B|Spawn_Ground|Taunt" (drops Spawn_Ground_Skeletons). Trial export: Skeleton_Minion 669 KB vs 557 KB now (about +0.45 MB for all four; Taunt 16 KB and Running_B 17 KB are optional).
Spawn_Ground (1.30 s): the root scales up from 0 (0.44 at 0.2 s), the skeleton jumps out (head 1.66 H at 0.4 s), lands at 0.8 s and settles at 1.3 s, so it is visible from about 0.1 s. In addEnemyView, play it with action.timeScale = clip.duration / Math.max(0.4, e.rise) (about 1.44: lands at 0.55 s and settles exactly when the sim makes it dangerous), then a 0.15 s fade to the run. Rename it in ONE_SHOT.
game.js line 181: emit(g,'spawn',{x:e.x, z:e.z, id:e.id, flying}). Render: a pooled dark ground-crack decal (CircleGeometry r 0.55, opacity 0.6 -> 0 over 1.4 s, depthWrite false, polygonOffset) plus a new fx 'dust' kind with its own normal-blend material (14 particles, speed 0.6-1.8, life 0.35-0.6, size 0.18-0.34, drifting up). Audio: a low rumble, throttled to 0.15 s.
game.js line 79: 'Rogue_Hooded' -> ENEMY_TYPES.runner.model[0] (Skeleton_Rogue). Render: a non-flying enemy that appears with rise 0 scales in from 0.3 to 1 over 0.15 s, with a purple 'big' burst where the splitter died.

recommendations.title: Throw, catch and pickup body timing on the part-1 arm layer
recommendations.why: Even with the part-1 upper-body layer, starting Throw at 0.5 s puts the release frame (0.72 s) 0.22 s after the sim has already launched the projectile on the same step. The ×2 catch, the skill moment, and pickups have no body reaction at all.
recommendations.how:
Wind-up: main.js passes charging: input.firing() && projectile held to view.sync. While charging, the arm layer plays Throw from 0 at timeScale 2.5 and pauses at 0.50 s: the cocked pose, hand drawn back, reached 0.2 s after the press. On 'shoot': time = max(time, 0.60), timeScale 1.5, unpause. Release then happens 0.08 s after the tap and the follow-through ends at +0.5 s (shootT 0.5). Mages: Spellcast_Shoot from 0 at 1.2x (peak at +0.07 s). Fire-cancel (part 1): fade the arms back over 0.15 s.
Catch and boomerang return: export Interact (1.30 s, +17 KB per hero; the right hand reaches forward 0.53 H at chest height between 0.4 and 0.6 s). Play it on the arm layer from 0.42 s at 1.6x (0.55 s): the hand is out at the catch, then pulls the item in. Add a 60 ms freeze, trauma 0.2, a gold burst and the held-prop pop. While pendingMult = 2, pulse the hero's ground ring (mark) gold.
Pickup: PickUp from 0.30 s at 2.2x (hand lowest 0.09 s later, done in 0.45 s): full body when standing still, arm layer when running (if it looks like a bow while running, skip it there). With the part-1 vacuum, start it when the vacuum starts.
Shield block: additive Hit_A on the hero (chest flinches 32 deg at +0.1 s; checked over Running_A).
Gotcha: action.reset() does not restore timeScale, so set timeScale explicitly every time you play a clip.
What works without built-in masks in r169: (a) track-filtered clips (part 1); (b) additive actions (checked here: no jump at the start, exact return); (c) bone offsets after mixer.update(), e.g. twisting 'chest' toward the throw direction for one-handed mode.

recommendations.title: Match animation speed to movement speed (stop the sliding)
recommendations.why: KayKit chibi legs are short. Measured planted-foot speed at game scale: the hero's Running_A and strafes about 1.7 m/s, but the hero moves at 5.2 m/s (3x slide). Walking_Backwards 0.35 m/s vs 5.2 m/s when running backwards in third person (15x: he glides backwards as if on ice). Skeleton Walking_D_Skeletons 0.26 m/s vs grunts at 1.6-2.56 m/s (6-10x); tank 0.28 vs 1.1-1.76. Characters look weightless.
recommendations.how:
render.js sync: a natural-speed table per clip, {Running_A:1.7, Running_Strafe_Left:1.7, Running_Strafe_Right:1.7, Walking_Backwards:0.35} x (model height/1.3). Every frame set hero.action.timeScale = clamp(g.hero.moving/natural, 0.6, 1.9). At 5.2 m/s that gives a 0.42 s cycle with 1.6x slide left; mirror the same timeScale on the arm layer's locomotion action.
Running backwards faster than 2 m/s: try Running_A at timeScale -1.8 (LoopRepeat plays it backward) and keep Walking_Backwards below 1 m/s; check how it looks on the device. Alternative (balance call): in main.moveVector, scale stick-down input to 65% in third person.
Enemies: Running_B (exported in the recommendation above; 1.20 m/s at 1.25 m, 1.07 s cycle) for grunt/tank/splitter, Running_A (1.86 m/s) for runners. timeScale = clamp(measured speed / natural, 0.75, 2.0), with the speed taken as a 0.15 s moving average of position change, so the river slow-down and the black-hole pull show in the legs too.

recommendations.title: Wave clear, hero death and shield save as real moments (and fix running/moonwalking in place)
recommendations.why: The perk screen is semi-transparent, so the scene shows behind it. The sim is paused there, but g.hero.moving keeps its last value, so a hero who was running when the wave ended plays Running_A in place. After death the sim stops but the skeletons' walk clips keep playing, so they moonwalk in place behind the game-over card. The death itself is a flat 1.1 s cut to the menu.
recommendations.how:
sync: if (g.choosing) clip = 'Cheer' (1.67 s; both hands above the head from 0.2 to 1.4 s; loop it while the player chooses). Last kill of a wave: slowMo(0.3, 0.45 s) plus a 15% third-person camera push-in. main.js line 200: perk delay 650 -> 900 ms.
Death: game.js line 212: add by: e.id. main: freeze 0.15 s, then slowMo(0.35, 0.6 s). Count overTimer in real time and raise it to 1.4 s (line 195) so Death_A finishes landing. render: the hero turns to face the killer (Death_A then falls away from it); camera pushes in 30% over 0.8 s; keep a reference to the VignetteEffect and raise vignette.darkness 0.42 -> 0.8 (high quality); add a red CSS flash. The killer plays Taunt (1.03 s, from the export), the others Idle (fixes the moonwalk). Trauma 0.8.
Shield save: freeze 90 ms, trauma 0.55, additive Hit_A on the hero, the attacker thrown back with Death_C_Skeletons, and a blue sphere flash (r 0.9, scale 1 -> 1.6, opacity 0.6 -> 0 in 0.3 s). While charges remain, show a faint bubble or ring per charge on the hero (today only the HUD icon shows it).
Cheap extras: Cheer once when a hero is picked on the heroes screen; on a new record, switch to the showcase camera and play Cheer behind the result card.

recommendations.title: Sound and combo build-up: limiter, rising notes, whoosh/crunch/clunk, end-of-shot total
recommendations.why: Every weapon fires the same 880->220 Hz square-wave 'pew'. The kill blip climbs linearly and gets shrill (combo 6 = square 1020->1560 Hz). Spawns and drops make no sound. Nothing limits the volume: a black-hole explosion that kills 5 at once sums to about 1.4x full scale in the worst case (3.95 x master 0.35), which clips on the iPhone speaker. Combos exist only as '+N ×k' text.
recommendations.how:
audio.js: master -> DynamicsCompressor (threshold -14 dB, knee 10, ratio 8, attack 0.002, release 0.12) -> destination. Per-type throttle of 30 ms. Several kills in one step play one sound at the highest combo.
Kill: bone crunch (bandpass noise 1.8 kHz Q 1.2, 0.09 s) + thump (sine 140->55 Hz, 0.12 s) + a triangle note climbing the major pentatonic from G4, 392*2^(s/12) with s = 0,2,4,7,9,12,14,16,19,21.
Shoot: a whoosh for thrown props (bandpass noise swept 500->2500 Hz over 0.16 s), a sparkly zap for orbs. Optional in-flight whirr: noise with a gain wobble at the spin rate (about 3.2 Hz) until drop/catch.
New sounds: 'drop' clunk (triangle 220->90 Hz 0.09 s + noise), 'spawn' rumble (noise low-passed at 300 Hz, 0.3 s), a high 'shing' on catch on top of the existing arpeggio, and on death a low-pass sweep on the master (20 kHz -> 500 Hz in 0.3 s).
Combo UI: .pop.combo at 28/34/40 px for ×2/×3/×5+, gold -> orange -> magenta, a slight random tilt. When a shot ends (drop/catch/return) with 2+ kills, show a total popup at the hero, «Комбо ×4 · +100» (main.js sums kill.points since the last 'shoot'). A separate «КОМБО ×3!» banner element (not #banner, which is used for waves).
Haptics: navigator.vibrate does not exist in iOS Safari. The iOS 17.4+ <input type=checkbox switch> trick (tijnjh/ios-haptics, MIT) only fires on a real tap through a label, so it works on DOM buttons (perk cards, Play, hero pick) but not for kills or the canvas-driven fire button. Not tested on a device.

summary: All 7 locations are built the same way: a flat-colored 16x24 m plane inside an 80x80 m plane, a 0.5 m box rim, and 10-13 circle obstacles that layoutFor() scatters at random angles. Edge decor only ever goes beside the left and right walls; nothing is placed beyond the north wall that the camera faces at spawn. In third person the ground outside the arena takes about 23% of the screen today (plus 30% sky) and about 40% with the part-1 camera. It is bare ground ending in a hard horizon line, and the fog never matches the sky's horizon color (green fog under a blue sky in forest/river, black fog under a night sky in the 'dungeon'). The 'fortress' river has no fortress. In play, colliders don't match the models. Cars, gravestones, graves and rubble have 31-62% invisible collision. Crates, presents and containers let the projectile through 31-42% of their footprint. Trees bounce the projectile 0.35-0.5 m before their 0.21-0.27 m trunks, and two rock models are lower than the projectile's 0.6 m flight height. Round deflectors also make bank shots a lottery: a ±1° aim error spreads the rebound 17.7° off a pillar but 2.0° off a flat wall. The location rules are global and can't be seen on the map (ice everywhere, every wall a portal). I prototyped rounded-box colliders plus walk-around steering in a scratch copy of src (28/28 tests pass) and drafted 7 hand-authored mirrored layouts that pass spawn-area, gap, spawn-lane and stuck-enemy checks. With those, plus instanced perimeter dressing in three height bands, kit floors and fog matched to each sky, every location can look like a place and play like a designed table, using only CC0 models already in assets/ or the KayKit packs. Nothing here was checked on an iPhone. All numbers come from node runs of the real simulation and GLB data, plus the existing SwiftShader screenshots.

recommendations.title: Make colliders match the models: rounded-box solids plus walk-around steering
recommendations.why: The projectile is the whole game, and today it bounces off air. Measured as the share of each collision circle with no model inside it: 37% beside cars, 62% in front of gravestones, 31% for graves, 45% for rubble. Trees use canopy-sized circles (r 0.6-0.7 m) around trunks that are 0.21-0.27 m wide at the 0.6 m flight height. Meanwhile the projectile visibly flies through the corners of crates, presents and containers (31-42% of their footprint is outside the circle). rock_single_A (0.32 m tall, river) and rock_largeA (0.47 m, forest) bounce a projectile that visibly passes over them. Flat faces also make bank shots learnable: in the simulation a ±1° aim error spreads the rebound 2.0° off a flat wall but 17.7° off a 0.5 m pillar. This change also makes walls, fences, parked cars and corridors possible at all.
recommendations.how:
(a) weapons.js: export solidContact(o, px, pz, pr) for a rounded box {x, z, rot, hx, hz, r}. hx = hz = 0 is today's circle; one of them 0 is a capsule. Rotate (px - x, pz - z) by -rot (same sense as three.js rotation.y), clamp to ±hx/±hz, normal = (local - clamped) rotated back, pen = r + pr - dist. If the center is inside the core, leave through the nearest face. Make bounce() and game.js pushOutOfSolids() call it. For circles the math is identical: a scratch copy of src/ with this change passes all 28 tests.
(b) game.js: add walk-around steering right after pushOutOfSolids(g, e). If a walker touches a solid and dot(toHero, n) < -0.2, step it along the face tangent (-n.z, n.x)·side at its chase speed. Pick `side` once on contact: the end of the solid's long axis (at ±(half + r + e.r + 0.05), +50 penalty if that end is outside the arena) with the shorter |enemy→end| + |end→hero|. Keep it in e.slide until the walker stops pressing, so it never flip-flops. For circles, act only when dead-centre (|tangential|/d < 0.05), so pillars and current difficulty stay as they are. Measured in the scratch sim: without steering a grunt never gets past a 2 m wall (30 s). With it, 2/3/5 m walls cost 5.1-5.6 / 6.0-6.7 / 9.0-10.1 s from 6 m away. Also clamp walkers to the arena like the hero. In spawnPos, nudge `along` in 0.15 m steps until the rise point is 0.2 m clear of solids (today up to 9.6% of spawn-lane points in the city rise inside an obstacle).
(c) locations.js: replace each obstacle's `r` with a shape:
- 'round': r = 0.46 × max footprint (pillars, barrels, snow trees, tents)
- 'trunk': r 0.32 (tree_oak, tree_default, tree_dead_large, tree_single_A)
- 'box': exact footprint, r 0.06 (crates, presents, containers, chests, dumpsters, gravestones)
- 'cap': r = half the width (cars, fences, walls, rubble)
Derive these from a generated src/footprints.js (native x/y/z of each GLB from accessor bounds, one line per model) times the entry's size, so the sim and render.js fit() use the same scale (drop the r*1.15 fit). fadeOccluders tests against max(hx, hz) + r; the table also gives part-1's occluder heights for free.
(d) Tests: a 45° shot off a wall leaves at 135°; a walker reaches a hero behind a 3 m wall; every solid is at least 0.6 m tall (fails today for rock_single_A and rock_largeA).

recommendations.title: Replace seeded scatter with hand-authored, mirrored layouts (drafts for all 7)
recommendations.why: Seeded scatter gives fixed but accidental maps: cars at random angles, five thin rubble pieces in the dungeon, four presents in winter. Tall trees and water towers stand in the middle, where they hide skeletons from the third-person camera (1-4 per location). Some walkers rise inside obstacles, and there are no lanes or landmarks. A designed table teaches shots: flat 'catch walls' send a straight throw back for the x2 catch, fences split the field into lanes, pillars act as bumpers. It also keeps an open space for running around the spawn (today the largest empty circle is 4.0-5.3 m and is not at the spawn). Every friend still plays the identical map, so scores stay comparable.
recommendations.how:
locations.js: give each location a fixed `layout` list and have layoutFor() map it with no RNG for solids. Keep seeded scatter only for decor. Entry format: [model, x, z, rotDeg, size in m (longest side) or {h}, shape]; M() adds the entry plus its mirror (-x, -rot).

Rules every layout follows:
1. Nothing within 2.6 m of the spawn (0,3).
2. Left/right mirror symmetry.
3. Solids clear of the walker spawn lanes (walkers rise 0.9 m inside each wall, r 0.4).
4. Every gap between solids, or between a solid and a wall, is either 0 or at least 1.0 m.
5. Long thin solids are at most 3 m long.
6. Anything taller than 1.6 m stays near the side walls, except thin pillars.
7. One flat catch wall faces a common shot line.
8. A landmark sits straight ahead (north) of the spawn camera.

Drafts (checked in the scratch sim):
- forest 'Поляна' (clearing): M tree_oak(-6.0,-7.5,h3.0,trunk); M tree_fat(-6.2,1.0,40°,h2.6,trunk); M tree_default(-5.8,8.8,h3.2,trunk); M hex/fence_wood_straight(-3.6,-5.0,10°,2.6,cap — splits 3 lanes); stump_round(0,-7,1.3,round); M rock_largeB(-2.6,-9.2,1.6,cap); M stump_round(-3.4,7.6,1.1,round).
- city 'Перекрёсток' (crossroads; N-S road |x|<3, E-W road z -7..-1): car_taxi(-1.5,-8.6,0°), car_police(1.5,9.2,0°), car_sedan(-5.2,-5.4,90°), car_sedan(5.2,-2.6,90°), car_police(0,-4.2,35°, crashed in the junction), all 2.8 m cap; M dumpster(-5.9,-9.6,90°,1.7,box); M dumpster(-5.9,5.0,90°,1.7,box); M box_A(-5.2,9.8,15°,0.8,box). The watertower moves to a roof outside.
- dungeon 'Колоннада' (colonnade): M pillar(-4.4,-8.6,1.0); M pillar_decorated(-4.4,-2.6,1.2); M pillar(-4.4,7.0,1.0), all round; M barrier(-4.4,-5.6,90°,2.4,cap); chest_gold(0,-9,1.2,box); M barrel_large(-2,-6,0.9); M crates_stacked(-6,2.4,1.3,box); M rubble_large(-2.4,9.2,20°,2.4,cap).
- winter 'Каток' (skating pond; the ellipse at (0,-4), rx 5, rz 4 stays empty): M tree-snow-a(-5.8,-9.4,h2.4); M tree-snow-b(-5.8,-2,h2.3); M tree-snow-c(-6,6,h2.4); snowman(0,-10,1.3); M present-a-cube(-3,7,20°,0.9,box); M present-a-cube(-2.6,-9.3,-10°,0.8,box); M rocks-large(-5.4,9.4,2.0).

Results against today's maps (2000 random ricochet throws; up to 100 walker runs from every side to 5 hero spots):
- 0 stuck walkers, 0 spawn-lane overlaps, no gap under 1 m.
- Worst extra arrival delay 1.0-2.9 s (river 4.9 s, which is the river slowdown, same as today).
- Predictable bounces (arena walls plus flat faces) go from 52-59% to 65-100%.
- Open space for running around the spawn: radius 5.0-6.5 m, centered on it (space 4.5 m).
- Tall solids in the middle: 0, except the thin dungeon pillars and the cemetery shrines.

Turn these checks into tests in tests/sim.test.mjs. Old personal bests were set on the old maps, so add a layout version to records and challenge links.

recommendations.title: Dress the outside in three height bands, instanced, with a landmark ahead of the spawn
recommendations.why: Measured for a portrait iPhone: with today's camera, 23% of the screen is ground outside the arena plus 30% sky. With the part-1 camera it is 40% (4% in the first metre, 9% at 1-5 m, 10% at 5-15 m, 8% at 15-40 m, 10% beyond) and only 1% sky. Today all of that is a flat plane, a hard horizon line, and nothing at the north end the camera faces when a run starts. A tree wall, a street of buildings, a dungeon hall, a village, a fortress, a fenced graveyard or a base turns each location into a place, and the menu orbit shows it first.
recommendations.how:
render.js setLocation: replace the four 0.5 m boxes with a dressing pass driven by a per-location `dress` spec in locations.js (decor only; seeded scatter is fine here). Bands, measured from the walls:
- Band 0 (0-1 m): a continuous low rim at most 0.9 m tall right on the wall line, so the projectile visibly bounces off it.
- Band 1 (1-4.5 m): props at most 1 m tall. The part-1 camera can be up to 4.5 m outside the walls, so nothing tall goes here and nothing needs fading.
- Band 2 (5 m and beyond): tall dressing and the landmark (6 m with today's 5.4 m camera distance).
- Band 3 (15-45 m): cheap big shapes that fade into fog.
The part-1 pitch shows only about 3° above the horizon, so the outside is seen from above. Run the floor out to about 15 m and put props on it; landmark tops at 7-8 m or less are what shows at the top edge.

Draw each model as one THREE.InstancedMesh with castShadow off. First share one material per kit: every KayKit GLB embeds its own copy of the same 1024x1024 atlas (12 identical copies per kit in assets/city, dungeon, halloween, hex and space), because GLTFLoader caches textures per file. That is about 5.3 MB of GPU memory per copy, and none are freed while the loader `cache` holds them. In prepare(), swap each mesh's material for the first one seen for that kit and dispose the duplicate map. Budget: at most 40k extra triangles and 12 extra draw calls per location (one skeleton is 5.3k triangles). The low quality setting skips bands 1 and 3.

Per location (new GLBs from the scratch KayKit packs via glTF-Transform, all CC0):
- forest: rim of plant_bushLarge hedge every 1.1 m; band 1 grass_large, mushroom_redGroup, rock_largeB, stump_round; band 2 three staggered rows of tree_default/oak/fat/cone (tree_cone is unused today), 2.6-4 m tall, every 2.2 m; landmark tree_oak 8 m tall at (0,-18); band 3 hex hills_A_trees x6.
- city: road tiles (scale 3, 6 m) run out of all four sides to 40 m; striped barrier boxes 0.6 m tall across the four road mouths, bush and sidewalk rim elsewhere; band 1 streetlight every 8 m, bench, trash_A/B, firehydrant; band 2 building_A-H (scale 3: 6 m footprint, 5-9 m tall) lining the streets from 5 m out; landmark building_H with the watertower on its roof, closing the north street at (0,-24); parked car_hatchback/stationwagon outside.
- dungeon: no sky; rim of barrier/barrier_column (scale 0.75: 3 m long, 0.8-1 m tall); band 2 hall walls 5 m out (wall, wall_arched, wall_window_open, wall_pillar at scale 0.75 = 3x3 m, about 40 pieces) with torch_mounted on every second piece and banner_patternA_red; landmark stairs at (0,-18) between two banners.
- winter: rim of snow-pile scaled into 2.6 x 0.5 m snowbanks; band 1 lanterns with flames, sled, presents; band 2 two rows of tree-snow-a/b/c, 2.5-4 m, plus 4-6 hex building_home_A/B_blue cottages at 7-12 m; landmark a 6 m tree-snow-a 'town tree' with presents and lanterns at (0,-18); band 3 hex mountain_A/B/C x6.
- river: make the Water plane 80 m long so the river runs into the fog on both sides; rim of fence_wood_straight except over the water; band 1 waterplant_A/B reeds and rocks on both banks, waterlily_A (in assets, unused today) and waterlily_B on the water; band 2 the fortress: wall_straight + wall_corner_A_outside + 3 building_tower_A_red (scale 3: 6 m segments, 3.3 m tall) along z -18, and building_castle_red (scale 3: 6 x 12 x 6.8 m) at (0,-24); trees_A/B_large clusters on the other sides; band 3 mountain_A_grass_trees.
- cemetery: rim of fence + fence_pillar (scale 0.4: 1.6 m long, 0.9 m tall), fence_gate where the path meets the north wall; band 1 more graves outside (gravemarker_A, grave_B, candles, pumpkins); band 2 tree_dead_medium/small, tree_pine_orange_large, post_lantern pairs along the path; landmark arch_gate at (0,-17) with the crypt (scale 0.6) at (0,-21).
- space: rim of portal fields (see the rules recommendation) between `lights` pylons every 4 m; band 1 rock_A/B, solarpanel, cargo_B; band 2 basemodule_A/C linked by tunnel_straight_A, structure_tall, windturbine_tall, spacetruck; landmark landingpad_large with lander_A at (0,-19); band 3 a crater rim of terrain_tall/terrain_slope blocks (12-28 triangles each).

recommendations.title: Turn each location's rule into a place on the map
recommendations.why: Today the rules are global and invisible. Ice makes the whole arena slippery (the joystick takes about 0.6 s to respond everywhere). The river is a featureless strip. The cemetery's 'out of nowhere' is just walls in fog. Every space wall is a portal, so space has the longest ricochet flights of any location (11.3 m mean drop distance), and the aim line draws a straight 23 m line across the arena whenever a shot wraps. Spatial rules give real choices (cross the ice or not, take the bridge, stay away from the graves, aim for the portal gate) and make each location card's description visible in the level itself.
recommendations.how:
winter: rule.ice = {x: 0, z: -4, rx: 5, rz: 4}. game.js uses friction 1.6 only while the hero is inside the ellipse (14 elsewhere), and weapons.js stepProjectile lets the dropped projectile slide (0.6) only on the ice (6 elsewhere). Draw the pond as a glossy ellipse (MeshStandardMaterial roughness 0.15, envMap = sky). desc 'Каток: на льду скользишь, снаряд катится'.

river: rule.river.bridges = [-4.5, 4.5] with half-width 1.3, so inRiver(g, x, z) is false on a bridge. Place two hex building_bridge_A (scale 2: 2.7 x 3.8 m; the deck sits at y≈0 and the piers go below the water plane) at (±4.5, -1.5). Skeletons wade straight through (no pathfinding) and bunch up slowed in the water, which sets up combos, while the hero crosses fast on the bridges. desc 'Река замедляет всех — по мосту быстрее'.

cemetery: rule.graves = the 12 grave spots, 0.9 m in front of each headstone. In game.js spawnPos, walkers from the left/right sides rise from the grave on that side whose z is nearest along·D and that is at least 4 m from the hero (otherwise the next one). Put floor_dirt_grave under each. The 0.9 s harmless rise and the Spawn_Ground_Skeletons clip stay as they are. desc 'Туман: скелеты встают из могил'.

space: rule.wrap = {x: 4, z: 6}. bounce() wraps only when a wall is crossed within |x| < 4 (north/south walls) or |z| < 6 (side walls), and reflects elsewhere, so walls become useful again. Mark the gates with a glowing additive field 1.2 m tall (a canvas stripe texture scrolled in render()) between two `lights` pylons.
Bug to fix: render.js setAim draws the preview as one THREE.Line, so each wrap draws a straight line across the arena (measured: 23.0 m and 15.2 m segments for one shot). Switch to LineSegments, skip point pairs with |Δx| > W or |Δz| > D, add a second aimEnd ring at the exit point, and emit a 'portal' event so fx.burst('ring') fires at both the entry and the exit.

dungeon: keep the darkness rule and give it structure. Put torch_mounted on the nave side of the 6 pillars and on the hall walls, each with an additive radial 'light pool' quad on the floor (one InstancedMesh, no extra lights): a lit nave and dark aisles. Raise the 10-flame cap in fx.setFlames to 14, or keep the 10 nearest the north end.

city (optional, needs the balance pass): skeletons come down the streets. Snap top/bottom spawns to |x| ≤ 2.4 and left/right spawns to z -6.4..-1.6, so they arrive in lines along roads lined with bank-wall cars. desc 'Скелеты идут по улицам — машины держат рикошет'.

recommendations.title: Floors from kit tiles or a painted ground texture, plus contact shadows
recommendations.why: The floor fills about 60% of the screen, and in all 7 locations it is one flat color. On the low quality setting (no shadow map) objects look like they float. Tiles, paths, river banks and the pond tell the player where they are and where to go, and dark contact patches under each obstacle anchor it even without shadows.
recommendations.how:
render.js: build the floor from a per-location `floor` spec in locations.js, instanced like the perimeter.
- dungeon: floor_tile_large (scale 0.75 = 3 m tiles) over the arena and the hall (about 100 instances of 188 triangles), with roughly every 6th tile swapped for floor_tile_small_broken_A or the weeds variant by seeded RNG.
- cemetery: Halloween floor_dirt (scale 1 = 4 m tiles), path_A-D stones (about 0.95 m) along x = 0 from the gate to the spawn, floor_dirt_grave under each grave spawn.
- city: road_straight, road_junction at (0,-4), road_straight_crossing at (0,1) and (±6,-4), and base tiles for sidewalks (scale 3 = 6 m tiles).
- forest, river, winter, space: a CanvasTexture painter (1024x1536 for the arena = 64 px/m, seeded like waterNormals()): base color plus two layers of noise. Forest gets a light dirt path up the middle lane from the spawn; river gets 0.8 m sand banks along both shores and dirt paths to the bridges; winter gets snow with blue noise and the ice ellipse; space gets rust-colored ground with crater rings and pad markings around the hub.

Contact shadows for every location: one plane at y 0.012 with a canvas of soft dark patches under each solid (radius about 0.7 × footprint) plus a 0.6 m darkening along the walls, using MultiplyBlending and depthWrite false.

Outer ground: replace the 80x80 plane with CircleGeometry(110, 48) using the floor material darkened ×0.8, so its edge always lies past the fog's far distance.

recommendations.title: Fog, light and sky per location so the ground fades into the horizon
recommendations.why: Every screenshot shows a hard line where the 80 m ground plane ends against the sky: with fog at 24-60 m the plane's edge is only about 25-70% fogged, and the sky background is not fogged at all. The fog color doesn't match the sky's horizon in any location. Sampled horizon colors: day #b2c6f2 vs forest fog #bfe3a8 (green) and river fog #c9dcae; morning #f9ddc4 vs winter #dfeaf3; alien #d8c5e9 vs space #e0b9a0; night #2f3b6b vs dungeon #15131b and cemetery #2a2f38. The hemisphere light's ground color is the same green 0x445533 on snow, asphalt and the space station, and the dungeon has a night sky.
recommendations.how:
locations.js: add a per-location `look` object, applied in render.js setLocation: hemi.color/groundColor/intensity, sun.color/intensity/position, scene.fog, and scene.background = loc.sky ? skyTexture : new THREE.Color(fog). Fog color = the sky's horizon color. Starting values (fog given as near-far in m):
- forest: fog 0xb2c6f2, 30-72; hemi 0xdde8ff / 0x5b7a3c, 1.3; sun 0xfff2d8, 2.3.
- city: fog 0xb6c4e4, 28-70; hemi 0xdde4ee / 0x6a6c72, 1.3; sun 0xffffff, 2.2.
- dungeon: no sky, background = fog 0x0b0a10, 9-28; hemi 0x6b5c8f / 0x16121c, 0.45; sun 0x9fa8ff, 0.3; heroLight 40 (as now).
- winter: fog 0xf6dcc8, 28-72; hemi 0xfff1e6 / 0xc9d9ea, 1.15; sun 0xffd3a8, 2.0, low from (-12, 7, 5) for long shadows; bloom 0.25 (as now).
- river: fog 0xb2c6f2, 32-78 (keeps the castle at 24-32 m readable); hemi 0xdde8ff / 0x6b8a4a, 1.35; sun 0xfff4e0, 2.3.
- cemetery: background = fog 0x262c3e, 8-22 (part-1's near distance of 8); hemi 0x8a98c8 / 0x1e2418, 0.55; moonlight sun 0xa9b8ff, 0.9, from behind (6, 12, -6) for silhouettes; flame and lantern particles with fog: false so the lights glow through the fog.
- space: fog 0xd8c5e9, 30-75; hemi 0xf0d8ff / 0x8a4a36, 1.25; sun 0xffd9c0, 2.4.
Tune on the iPhone.
